headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift certain grid infrastructure and capacity costs from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers, to reduce household utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumers, consumer advocacy groups, Dominion Energy.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aim to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics, including the bill's patron, expressed concern that the governor's amendments might weaken the original intent of shifting costs.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water supplied to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing data for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales to data centers, providing more transparency on water usage, though specific facility data remains protected. This legislation aims to fill a data gap for state environmental quality and water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise impacts and allows localities to demand information on potential impacts to water, agriculture, forests, and parks when siting new data centers.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: A Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law. Here's What It Does, and What It Doesn't
news_summary: Virginia's new law, effective July 1, 2026, requires developers to study noise and utilities to disclose substations for new data center sites, but it does not set specific limits on either. The legislation aims to provide localities with more information for zoning decisions, addressing concerns from communities experiencing data center growth.
